To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

young and middle-aged Japanese males with metabolic syndrome who had been viewed not to require medication had higher all-cause mortality and cardiovascular disease event rates than those without metabolic syndrome.

young and middle-aged men with MS who were considered not needing medication already had an increased rate of all-cause, cardiovascular and ischemic heart disease death, depending on the specific combination and number of components of the syndrome.

the association between subjects with MS who were considered not requiring medication and all-cause death, IHD and cardiovascular disease was significant and depended on the specific MS components in a young and middle-aged Japanese population.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between MS and all-cause death, CVD and IHD in young and middle-aged men
a cohort study of Japanese men who were not on any medication and who had been diagnosed as having MS by their attending physicians, and who were followed up for 7.5 years.
the importance of early intervention in subjects with MS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MS is an independent risk factor for all-cause mortality and CVD in young and middle-aged Japanese males.
MS is an indicator of increased mortality risk, and that the risk is higher for subjects with MS defined by Japanese than by NCEP ATPLI III criteria.

the metabolic syndrome, as defined by the modified Japanese criteria, is a risk factor for all-cause death, IHD, and CVD, even among young and middle-aged Japanese who were considered by their physicians not to require medication.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MS was associated with a higher risk of all-cause and cardiovascular mortality, and that the combination of three components was associated with the highest risk.
the presence of MS, even without any medication, is a risk factor for all-cause mortality and CVD.
MS is a strong risk factor for cardiovascular diseases and should be considered as a risk factor even in young and middle-aged men.
The main takeaway from our work is that
metabolic syndrome is an important risk factor for all-cause mortality and cardiovascular events, even in young and middle-aged Japanese subjects.
the metabolic syndrome should be considered a serious condition in middle-aged men, even when they are not receiving any medications.
metabolic syndrome is a serious risk factor for all-cause mortality and CVD even in young- and middle-age subjects.
